editorial:
Imagine living on a tiny, windy island in the Orkneys where your only job is hunting birds and keeping old family stories alive. That is the world of Isla and Sandy, two siblings who treat anyone from the mainland like a monster. They have a great bond and a funny way of looking at the world, which makes the first half of the film feel like a cozy, quirky adventure. The vibe is a mix of a family drama and a fish-out-of-water comedy that really draws you into their strange, isolated way of life.

You will love how the awkward council worker clashes with the siblings, as the acting makes the tension feel real but funny. While the middle part slows down a bit, the emotional payoff at the end is totally worth it. It is a perfect pick for a rainy Sunday afternoon when you just want a story with a lot of heart.
endingExplained: In the end, the council worker realizes that the siblings are the only ones keeping the island's history alive. Instead of forcing them to leave, he helps them find a legal loophole to stay on their land. The twist is that he actually grew up in a similar small town and felt the same loss. They all end up forming an unlikely friendship, and the movie closes with them hunting birds together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky family stories and beautiful scenery.
